description: A mono delay meant to be swept: the feedback path is bit-crushed and downsampled, the feedback fades out and back in around every wrap so the time can be moved without clicking

params.text: Scales the TIME control input before it is added to the TIME knob
Trims the delay time by up to 99 milliseconds either way, added to the TIME knob
Scales the FINE control input before it is added to the FINE knob
Sets the delay time, 0.1 to 4 seconds
Sets how coarsely the feedback path is quantised: fully up leaves it alone, and turning down steps the signal to fewer and fewer levels
Scales the CRUSH control input, which is subtracted from the CRUSH knob rather than added to it
Scales the FB control input before it is added to the FB knob
Sets how much of the delay line is fed back into itself; the knob is squared before use and reaches a little past unity, so the repeats can build rather than only fade
Sets how much of the incoming signal is written into the delay line
Scales the INPUT control input before it is added to the INPUT knob
Scales the DRY control input before it is added to the DRY knob
Sets how much of the untouched input reaches the output
Adds its own value squared to the WET knob, and only while a cable is in the WET control input; the voltage on that cable is never read
Sets how much of the delay line reaches the output

inputs.text: Added to the TIME knob through the TIME CV knob, 0.98 seconds per volt at full amount
Added to the FINE knob through the FINE CV knob, about 20ms per volt at full amount
Subtracted from the CRUSH knob through the CRUSH CV knob, 0.8 of a step per volt at full amount
Added to the FB knob through the FB CV knob, 0.12 per volt at full amount, before the total is squared
Added to the INPUT knob through the INPUT CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
Added to the DRY knob through the DRY CV knob, a tenth per volt at full amount
The voltage here is never read; patching any cable into it makes the WET CV knob add its own square to the WET knob, and that is all it does
The signal to be delayed, summed to one channel if the cable is polyphonic

outputs.text: The dry and delayed signals mixed by the DRY and WET knobs, one channel
A 1ms trigger each time the delay line wraps round, for firing envelopes in step with the repeats

notes: the CRUSH control input reaches only the sample-rate reduction in the feedback path; the bit-depth quantisation is taken straight from the knob, so no cable can change it
the feedback is faded to nothing over the samples left before the delay line wraps and faded back in over the next 250 samples, which is what lets the TIME knob be swept without clicks
the module is monophonic: a polyphonic input is summed and both outputs carry one channel
